corpus.title: OPINION: Yes, Swedish immigrants vote in their own interests – just like other voters
corpus.signal_text:
Since the Sweden Democrats are an ethno-nationalist party with a track record of pointing to immigration as the source of all of the country’s ills, it didn’t come as a big surprise that, in the wake of their first-ever electoral decrease, top party members blamed immigrant voters.
Some blamed new citizens – those who had been granted citizenship over the past four Tidö years, against the wishes of the Sweden Democrats, who wanted a total freeze on new citizenships.
Others targeted a specific ethnic-religious minority group (guess which one!), saying that their votes had influenced, or swayed the election.
This includes Sweden Democrat party leader Jimmie Åkesson, who, in his post-election press conference this morning, said that the Social Democrats and the Left Party "mobilised Islamist voters."
Perhaps more surprising was that a Moderate MP (admittedly, one on the rightward end of the party) did something similar. In an article in the British magazine The Spectator, Fredrik Kärrholm referred the 97.6 percent vote share of the Social Democrats and Left Party in Malmö’s immigrant-heavy Rosengård neighbourhood as “Saddam Hussein numbers.”
Public broadcaster SVT and The Local’s Richard Orange did a fact check on some of these claims, finding that while the claim about who new citizens voted for was completely unfounded and, in fact, unverifiable, Swedish voters with “foreign” backgrounds did indeed heavily favour the Social Democrats and the Left Party – the two largest parties on the opposite side of the political spectrum from the Sweden Democrats.
To which I say, “So what?”
Kärrholm’s Spectator article is entitled “Did demographics decide the Swedish election?”, a headline which implies that particular demographic groups having a decisive influence on elections is somehow new or unusual.
Did demographics decide the Swedish election in 2022, when, as The Local found out, foreign-born voters with non-European backgrounds voted more to the right than in the 2026 election?
Maybe!
Did demographics change the face of Swedish politics over the last 12 years as rural working-class men threw their support in force behind the Sweden Democrats?
Yes!
That is democracy. Particular demographic groups regularly sway elections.
